source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 一.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–1 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies one ordered stroke for 一. Median 1 runs from the left of the square rightward across the middle, rising very slightly before it settles. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions and pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 七.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–2 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 七. Median 1 crosses from the left edge to the right, rising slightly; median 2 begins high on the right, descends, turns along the foot and lifts into a hook. Two strokes for seven, which is the point the course makes about stroke count and meaning having parted company.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 三.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 三, all horizontal, ordered top, middle, bottom. Median 3 is markedly the widest, which is what stops the character reading as a stack of identical bars. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions and pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 上.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 上. Median 1 descends the central vertical from the top toward the base. Median 2 separately starts at the vertical and draws the short middle horizontal left-to-right. Median 3 separately draws the long base horizontal left-to-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all three medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, both intervening lifts, and the short-before-long horizontal contrast; Noto's vertical is straighter and both horizontals are flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 不.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 不: a top horizontal from left to right, a separately started long falling stroke from the upper centre down-left, a separately started central vertical, and a separately placed right-falling dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all four medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, directions, and three intervening lifts; Noto's long falling stroke is smoother and its right dot is broader than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 个.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 个. Medians 1–2 are exactly 人 — the same left-falling then right-falling pair, from the same peak, that the first writing lesson in this track taught — and median 3 is a single vertical hung beneath the junction. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 你.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–7 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies seven ordered strokes for 你. Medians 1–2 draw 亻 first: a left-falling stroke followed by a separately started vertical. Median 3 restarts at the upper right and falls down-left; median 4 restarts below it, crosses rightward, then hooks down-left without lifting; median 5 restarts at the centre, descends, then hooks left without lifting; medians 6–7 separately draw the lower-left dot down-left and the lower-right dot down-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those seven ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, both joined hooks, the component order, and six intervening pen lifts; Noto's right horizontal and hooks are squarer than the source medians, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 儿.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–2 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 儿. Median 1 starts near the upper centre and falls down-left; median 2 restarts at the upper right, descends nearly vertically, bends right along the base, then hooks upward without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those two ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the second stroke's unbroken bend and hook, and one intervening pen lift; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 再.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 再. Median 1 draws the top horizontal left-to-right. Median 2 separately descends the left side. Median 3 restarts at the upper left, crosses the frame's top, turns down the right side, then hooks left at the base without lifting. Median 4 descends the central vertical, median 5 draws the inner horizontal, and median 6 closes with the long bottom horizontal left-to-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, both turns inside the enclosing third stroke, the close-last rule, and five intervening lifts; Noto's frame is squarer and its bottom horizontal is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 十: median 1 crosses from left to right, median 2 descends through its centre. Horizontal before vertical, the same order 三 and 四 already used. The character is the lower component of 早 and appeared in this course as a part of that character for thirteen chapters before it was taught on its own.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 口.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–3 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 口. Median 1 starts at the upper left and descends the left side; median 2 restarts near the upper left, crosses the top from left to right, turns without lifting, then descends the right side; median 3 restarts at the lower left and closes the bottom from left to right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the joined corner, and two intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 名. Medians 1–3 draw 夕 first: an upper left-falling stroke, a separately started horizontal that continues down-left without lifting, and a separately placed inner down-right dot. Medians 4–6 then draw 口: the left vertical, a separately started top horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, and the closing bottom horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, both joined turns, and five intervening lifts; Noto's 夕 sweep is broader and 口 is squarer than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 吗.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 吗. Medians 1–3 draw the left 口 in the same order the standalone character uses: its left vertical, its joined top and right sides, and its closing bottom horizontal, all inside the upper-left third of the square. Medians 4–6 then draw 马: a horizontal that turns down at the right, a long stroke that turns twice and hooks, and a wide finishing horizontal that runs almost the full width of the character and is the widest stroke in it. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, directions, the two joined corners and five intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 呢. Medians 1–3 draw the left 口 in the same order the standalone character uses and in the same upper-left third of the square that 吗 puts it in. Medians 4–6 draw 尸 — a turning top stroke, a horizontal, and a long left-falling stroke that runs past the bottom of 口 — and medians 7–8 draw 匕 tucked inside it. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all eight medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the three internal turns and seven intervening lifts; Noto sets 尸's long falling stroke slightly steeper than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 和. Medians 1–5 draw 禾: the short top left-falling stroke, the horizontal, the long central vertical, then the left-falling and right-falling pair that finish it. Medians 6–8 draw 口 on the right in the same order the standalone character uses. Left component complete before the right one begins. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all eight medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the joined corner in 口 and seven intervening lifts; Noto compresses 禾's final right-falling stroke into a dot, as the source graphic does, because 口 stands beside it.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 喜, and they descend the character in four bands: medians 1–3 the 士 at the top, medians 4–6 a 口, medians 7–8 the short pair beneath it, median 9 the single widest horizontal in the character, and medians 10–12 the closing 口. Top before bottom throughout, and each 口 is built left side, joined top-and-right, closing floor — the order the reader already writes. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 四.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–5 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies five ordered strokes for 四. Medians 1–2 build the outer box exactly as 口 does — the left side, then the top and right in one turning stroke; medians 3–4 are the two pieces inside it; median 5 closes the bottom last. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions and pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

and turning up to the right at its foot
lift, then close the bottom with a horizontal héng stroke from left to right

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 国.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–8 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 国. Medians 1–2 open the outer frame, medians 3–7 finish every stroke of 玉 inside it, and median 8 closes the frame along the bottom. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians share the coordinate system used for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. The ductus uses those ordered source medians directly; the vendored Noto Sans SC outline can differ in width and proportion from the Arphic-derived source graphics.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies three ordered strokes for 女. Median 1 starts near the upper centre, makes a short down-right entry, bends down-left to the lower-left junction, then turns without lifting and sweeps down-right to finish; median 2 restarts at the upper right and falls down-left; median 3 restarts at the left edge and crosses the middle from left to right. This learner path adapts those three ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the first stroke's internal turn, and two intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 好.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 好. Medians 1–3 draw 女 first: a bent stroke descends down-left and sweeps right without lifting, a separately started stroke falls down-left, and a separately started horizontal crosses left-to-right. Medians 4–6 then draw 子: a horizontal turns down-left without lifting, a separately started vertical descends and hooks left without lifting, and a separately started middle horizontal crosses left-to-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those six ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, 女-before-子 component order, all three joined turns, and five intervening pen lifts; Noto's 子 top turn is more angular and its vertical hook is flatter than the source medians, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 家.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 家. Medians 1–3 complete 宀 from the top dot through the hooked roof; medians 4–10 then complete the lower body from its top horizontal through the central curve, three left-falling strokes, and final right-falling stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the roof-before-body order, each unbroken turn, and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

lift, then draw its left-falling stroke
lift, then descend the centre and curve to a hook at the base without lifting
lift, then add the short left-falling stroke beside the centre
lift, then add the longer left-falling stroke below it
lift, then add the lower left-falling stroke
lift, then finish with the long right-falling nà stroke

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 岁. This learner path adapts all seven medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, directions, both joined hooks, and six lifts; Noto's long slash is more curved and its crossing strokes are more geometric than the Arphic-derived source graphics.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 日. Median 1 starts at the upper left and descends the left side; median 2 restarts near the upper left, crosses the top from left to right, turns without lifting, then descends the right side; median 3 restarts at the left edge and crosses the middle from left to right; median 4 restarts at the lower left and closes the bottom from left to right. This learner path adapts those four ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, the joined top-right corner, the inside-before-close order, and three intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 早. Medians 1–4 complete 日 first: the left side, a separately started top horizontal that turns down the right side without lifting, the middle horizontal, and the separately closing bottom horizontal. Median 5 then draws 十's horizontal left-to-right, and median 6 separately descends its vertical through the horizontal. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving the complete 日-before-十 component order, the joined top-right turn, and five intervening lifts; Noto's 日 is squarer and 十's horizontal is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 是. Medians 1–4 draw 日 first: its left vertical, joined top and right sides, inner horizontal, and closing bottom horizontal. Medians 5–9 then draw a wide horizontal, central vertical, short lower-right horizontal, lower-left falling stroke, and long finishing stroke down-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all nine medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, directions, the joined top-right corner, and eight intervening lifts; Noto's lower finishing stroke is broader and flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 有.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 有. Medians 1–2 are the horizontal and the long left-falling stroke that cross at the top, in that order — horizontal before left-falling, the rule 大 and 六 already showed. Medians 3–6 build 月 beneath: left side, then the joined top-and-right that hooks at the base, then the two inner horizontals, so the enclosure is closed before it is filled. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the joined corner, the base hook and five intervening lifts; Noto's 月 is slightly narrower than the source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 欢.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–6 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies six ordered strokes for 欢. Medians 1–2 draw 又 exactly as 对 draws it, which is why the two characters are taught near each other; medians 3–6 draw 欠 as a short left-falling stroke, a hooked horizontal, then the long left-falling and right-falling pair that carry the whole right half. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all six medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the internal turn in 又, the hook in 欠 and five intervening lifts; Noto's final right-falling stroke reaches further right than the Arphic-derived source graphic's.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies eight ordered strokes for 的. Medians 1–5 draw 白: a short left-falling stroke, then the box built as 百's was — left side, joined top and right, inner bar, closing floor. Medians 6–8 draw 勺: a left-falling stroke, a long stroke down the right side that hooks left at the base, and a dot placed last inside the enclosure. Outside before inside, and the dot is the final stroke. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all eight medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, the two joined corners and seven intervening lifts; Noto's 勺 is narrower than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order and that the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. The ductus preserves that ordered sequence while fitting its learner pen paths to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline, whose width and proportions differ from the Arphic-derived source graphics.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 见.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–4 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies four ordered strokes for 见. Median 1 descends the frame's left side. Median 2 separately draws the top horizontal and turns down the right side without lifting. Median 3 draws the inner left-falling leg. Median 4 separately descends the second leg, bends right along the base, and finishes with an upward hook without lifting. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all four medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, the frame-before-legs sequence, all three joined turns across the top-right frame and vertical-bend hook, and three intervening lifts; Noto's upper frame is squarer and its hooked leg is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 讠.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–2 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies two ordered strokes for 讠. Median 1 starts at the upper left and draws the dot down-right; median 2 restarts at the left edge, rises slightly across the short horizontal, turns without lifting to descend, then turns again without lifting and finishes up-right. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those two ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their directions, both turns inside the second stroke, and one intervening pen lift; Noto's middle horizontal and descent are squarer than the source median, and stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.

source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 请. Medians 1–2 draw 讠: a down-right dot, then a separately started short horizontal that turns down and finishes up-right without lifting. Medians 3–10 draw 青: two upper horizontals, a central vertical, a wide middle horizontal, the lower left side, a separately started lower top horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks left at the base without lifting, then two inner horizontals. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all ten medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, all four internal turns across 讠 and 青, and nine intervening lifts; Noto's 青 horizontals are flatter and its lower enclosure is squarer than the Arphic-derived source graphic.

source.citation: Hanzi Writer Data 谢.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–12 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019)
source.variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies twelve ordered strokes for 谢. Medians 1–2 draw 讠: a down-right dot, then a separately started short horizontal that turns down and finishes up-right without lifting. Medians 3–9 draw 身: an upper falling stroke, the left side, a separately started top horizontal that turns down the right side and hooks left at the base without lifting, two inner horizontals, a wide lower horizontal, and a lower falling stroke down-left. Medians 10–12 draw 寸: a horizontal, a separately started vertical that hooks left at the base without lifting, and a final down-right dot. Make Me a Hanzi documents proper People's Republic of China stroke order and matching animation medians. This learner path adapts all twelve medians to Noto Sans SC while preserving their order, all five internal turns across 讠, 身, and 寸, and eleven intervening lifts; Noto's 身 enclosure is squarer and 寸's hook is flatter than the Arphic-derived source graphic.
